_: GENUINE TC2000 PERSONAL CRITERIA FORMULAS, AND WHAT THIS PRODUCT DOES WITH EACH. Not one line of this file was invented as a test input: every `source` under `accepted` and `refused` is a formula published by Worden or by a TC2000 practitioner, cited per case. A toy corpus proves that a parser parses; this one measures whether a member who already writes PCF can walk in.

_sources.worden-syntax-table: Worden/TC2000 Personal Criteria Formula syntax reference — the vendor's own published function and operator table (help.tc2000.com). The authority for which spellings exist, and for which of them are DIFFERENT FORMULAS wearing familiar names (RSI vs WRSI, WSTOC, MS, TSV).

_accepted: `native` is the SAME formula written in this product's own dialect. The rail is `astHash(pcf) === astHash(native)` — not that the PCF reader produces *a* tree, but that it produces the tree the engine already runs on both lanes at 1e-9. A PCF layer that produced its own trees would be a second numeric surface; this one produces none.
_refused: `guard` is the door that must fire and `at` is the source index the refusal must point at. ⛔ BOTH ARE ASSERTED. A refusal that arrives from the wrong door reads identically to the right one, and a refusal with no position is one a member cannot act on.

accepted.what: `STOCk.3.z` is the SLOW stochastic — %K smoothed over three bars. The smoothing is a moving average OVER the stochastic, not an argument to it, so it translates to this table without a new function
the smoothing a member wrote is neither dropped nor refused — dropping it would show them a DIFFERENT indicator under the name they typed

AROONUPx.z / AROONDOWNx.z. ⭐ THE SYNTAX IS WORDEN'S AND THE FORMULA IS CHANDE'S: the Worden table publishes `AROONUP(x, z)` with x=Period, z=Offset and NO formula at all, so the maths is cited to the published definition `Aroon-Up = ((25 - Days Since 25-day High)/25) x 100`. ⛔ THE WINDOW IS n+1 BARS, and that is arithmetic rather than a reading: Aroon's published range is 0-100, and over n bars "days since" maxes at n-1 so it could never print 0.
accepted.note: was refused as "an indicator family this table does not declare" until W2a.7 declared `aroonUp`/`aroonDown` on task 5's `highestbars`/`lowestbars`.

accepted.what: AROONDOWNx.z -- the OTHER leg, and not a duplicate of `aroon`. ⛔ IT EXISTS BECAUSE THE MUTATION SWEEP PROVED THE FIRST ROW DID NOT COVER IT: pointing `AROONDOWN` at `aroonUp` is a one-word edit yielding a perfectly plausible 0-100 column off the wrong field, and with only an `AROONUP` row in this corpus it stayed green. The two legs read DIFFERENT fields through OPPOSITE comparisons, so this row is the only place the mapping's DIRECTION is pinned.
accepted.note: `< 30` rather than `> 70` on purpose: an Aroon-Down reading is the mirror of an Aroon-Up one, so a row that asked the SAME question of both legs would still pass with the two columns swapped.

WSTOCx.y.z — a RANK, not a range. Worden publishes "Worden Stochastic = (100/n-1)(Rank)" on its own indicator page, where Rank is the ascending position of the newest close among the closes of the period; its worked example gives 25 where a standard stochastic gives 16.7. This table declares no rank function, so the formula is INEXPRESSIBLE rather than merely different. ⭐ UNBLOCKED BY ONE ENTRY: declare `rank(source, n)` and `WSTOC(x, y, z)` becomes `sma(100 / (x - 1) * rank(close, x), y)`.

⭐ TC2000's `RSIx.y.z` is NOT the 14-period Wilder RSI a scan usually means — the template table derives the Kaufman Efficiency Ratio from it and declares Wilder's separately as WRSIx.z. Mapping `RSI14` to our `rsi` would be a correct-looking number from the wrong indicator

OBVy.z — `y` is an SMA, so this is the mean OF A CUMULATIVE RUNNING TOTAL. TC2000's own page calls that level "statistically irrelevant, just as it would be with a cumulative advance/decline line", which is exactly the ground `_functions_excluded.obv` refuses on: a running total from the first bar is a fact about where the fetch started. ⛔ IT IS NOT `obvN(n)` — the bounded signed-volume SUM W2a.5 declared is a different quantity, and pointing this spelling at it would be the MIN/lowest trap.

ADX's dotted number is its SMOOTHING, and this table's `adx` uses one period for both. An unequal pair refuses rather than quietly returning a 14/14 ADX — a member who asked for 14/20 must not be shown a number that is not the indicator they asked for

_offset: ⭐ THE BAR OFFSET IS ENGINE-DEPENDENT AND THIS SECTION FLIPS WITH IT. PCF's `.z` suffix is its most-used feature, so these are the cases that decide whether a member notices a discrepancy. The expectation is DERIVED, not written: while `closedTable.json` declares no offset form, each must refuse at `pcf:offset` at the declared character; the moment it declares one, each must PARSE, carry the declared offset node, and still lint to a forward reach of 0. ⛔ Neither half may be skipped — a suite that only checked the refusal would go silently green the day the engine grew the capability and this reader failed to use it.
